best_for: PC gamers who own a PlayStation 2 and its discs and want to replay that library at higher resolutions, with save states, on a reasonably modern computer.

points.title: Most of the PS2 library plays
points.text: PCSX2 is a free, open-source PS2 emulator, and the project says most of the PS2 library is playable, many games at full speed. You can upscale, use save states and share virtual memory cards.

points.title: You must supply the BIOS
points.text: PCSX2 will not run games without a PS2 BIOS, and there is no open-source stand-in. The project's guide shows how to dump the BIOS from your own console, which can mean a softmod memory card or a burned DVD.

points.title: Check your CPU first
points.text: The minimum is a 64-bit x86 CPU with SSE4.1 and two cores, 8 GB of RAM and Vulkan 1.1, Direct3D 11 or OpenGL 3.3 graphics. Heavier games want AVX2 and four or more cores, and 32-bit systems are not supported.

points.title: Apple Silicon runs it through Rosetta
points.text: There is no native Arm build. On M-series Macs PCSX2 runs through Rosetta 2, and the project lists macOS 11 Big Sur as the minimum.

points.title: Older Windows is out
points.text: Windows 10 21H2 or newer is required; 7, 8 and early Windows 10 releases were dropped in past versions. The Windows installer is x64 and installs for all users.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is official
points.text: The x64 Flatpak on Flathub is verified as published by the PCSX2 team. The project also offers an AppImage, and both Wayland and X11 work.

points.title: Rolling back
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 5 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so older builds there come from the project's GitHub releases.
